details.statement_alignment: Conditional full CAS-07-C02 for every real 2x2 D under s>0, 0<=eta<1 and the declared Euclidean induced operator-norm bound; positive determinant and both singular-value bounds derived. No C01/C03/Jacobi or scientific admission.
universal_derivation: Let A=D-sI and q=s eta. The supplied Euclidean induced operator bound means ||Ax||_2<=q||x||_2 for every real x: for x!=0 apply its unit-vector definition to x/||x||_2; x=0 is immediate. Thus q>=0 and q<s from s>0 and 0<=eta<1.

The checked two-dimensional Lagrange sum-of-squares identity gives (u dot v)^2<=(u dot u)(v dot v), hence Cauchy-Schwarz and the Euclidean triangle inequality after squaring nonnegative norms. Apply it to Dx=sx+Ax for the upper bound; apply it to sx=Dx-Ax for the lower bound. Thus, for every x, (s-q)||x||_2<=||Dx||_2<=(s+q)||x||_2. No matrix Frobenius, row, column, entrywise, or indefinite norm enters.

G=D^T D is real symmetric and x^T G x=||Dx||_2^2>=0. Its characteristic discriminant is (G00-G11)^2+4G01^2>=0. For nonzero off-diagonal k, v=(k,lambda-G00) is a nonzero eigenvector whenever lambda is a characteristic root; when k=0 use standard basis eigenvectors. If roots coincide, the sum of squares forces k=0 and G00=G11. Hence both real eigenvalues have real nonzero eigenvectors, and their nonnegative square roots are precisely the two declared singular values.

Apply the universal vector inequalities to either eigenvector v of G. Because ||Dv||_2^2=lambda||v||_2^2 and both sides are nonnegative, s-q<=sqrt(lambda)<=s+q. This includes multiplicity, eta=0, and nonsymmetric D.

For every t in [0,1], D_t=sI+tA obeys ||D_t x||_2>=(s-tq)||x||_2, with s-tq=(s-q)+(1-t)q>0. Thus D_t has zero kernel and det(D_t)!=0 for every t. Its determinant is a continuous real polynomial in t; det(D_0)=s^2>0. The intermediate-value theorem therefore gives det(D)=det(D_1)>0. Positivity is derived here, not assumed.

The symbolic identity det(G)=det(D)^2 and det(D)>0 imply sigma_1 sigma_2=det(D). With lower=s-q>0, upper=s+q and each sigma_i in [lower,upper], the two checked cone decompositions prove lower^2<=sigma_1 sigma_2<=upper^2 using only nonnegative factors. The positive square root is monotone on nonnegative reals, so lower<=sqrt(det(D))<=upper. Substitute q=s eta to obtain exactly s(1-eta)<=sqrt(det(D))<=s(1+eta).
